Name: trace_distribution_so_n
Title: Statistical Analysis of Trace Distribution in Random SO(N) Matrices
Experiment: Generate a large number of random SO(N) matrices and analyze the distribution of their traces. Compare the empirical distribution to theoretical predictions, if available. Investigate how the distribution changes with N.

Name: eigen_spacing_so_n
Title: Level-Spacing Statistics of Haar-Random SO(N) Matrices and Comparison to the Circular Orthogonal Ensemble
Experiment: Extend experiment.py by adding a function eigen_level_spacings(M) that computes sorted eigen-phases (angles) of M, normalises nearest-neighbour spacings so the mean is 1, and returns all spacings. In the main loop, accumulate spacings across all samples. Also test uniformity of raw eigen-phases. For each chosen N (e.g., 3, 5, 10, 20), build a histogram of spacings, compute the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance between the empirical CDF and the Wigner surmise CDF p_W(s) = (π/2) s exp(-π s^2 / 4), and store results in JSON along with mean spacing. Save arrays of phases, spacings, and histogram counts for optional offline plotting.

Name: entry_concentration_so_n
Title: Entry-wise Concentration and Maximum Entry Statistics in Haar-Random SO(N) Matrices
Experiment: For N in [3,5,10,20,50], generate num_samples Haar-random matrices. Collect: (i) all entries; compute their empirical mean, variance, and Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance between sqrt(N)*entries and N(0,1). (ii) For each matrix, randomly sample 100 distinct column pairs, record their inner products; report overall mean and variance. (iii) Record the maximum absolute entry of each matrix; build its histogram and report mean and std, comparing mean*sqrt(N) to sqrt(2*log(N)). Store per-N statistics and raw arrays in JSON for later analysis.
